observations.statement: All 41 authorized model trials succeeded with null errors; previous_runtime_error is null. Earlier count/product/gradient/action/mean branches include scientific negatives, not failed training executions. Round12 submission notes preserve a repaired local harness extraction failure; current retrieval truncation and missing validator are separate preparation/availability issues.

Feature-only, pooled and target-aware references have AUC 0.6050036144838207, 0.6102261137080656 and 0.6133619861190683. Useful history signal is observed, without identifying behavior semantics as its cause.

Full behavior-count correction lowers pooling and DIN AUC; half correction helps pooling but still lowers DIN AUC. The weaker follow-up did not rescue the target-aware branch. Joint product restrictions improve the ordinary product adapter; separate restriction cells and their interaction prevent attributing the whole gain to one removal.

Aligned unit products improve aligned raw AUC; crossed normalization does little for AUC and worsens loss. The original full derivative beats detached, identity and unit-scale tangent rules, but later fixed-0.2 tangent/identity replacements approach full AUC. Precise adaptive scale and projection necessity are unestablished.

Whole-history mean is near full/fixed in AUC with worse Logloss. Chronological half-rotation, action-half and action-mean lose AUC; adjacent replacements recover in both groupings. These negative outcomes remain valid and rule-specific.

The ordering-by-offset AUC interaction is -0.0003459909071475975: chronological adjacent-minus-half is +0.00026890848463556605, rank adjacent-minus-half is -0.00007708242251203146. Rank-half leads AUC while rank-adjacent leads Logloss; the AUC reversal does not imply a matching loss reversal.

Round13 full and scale-half audits exactly reproduce their ancestor AUC, Logloss, population size and all 23 slice metrics/counts. The retained AUC incumbent is r0012-scale_half at 0.6151021885074872. The audit does not improve the incumbent or add a seed.

At each audited checkpoint, candidate-authored diagnostics report zero common-state forward logit discrepancy on first512 and probe32 inputs. Rotations conserve scale sums/squared sums to about 2.05e-7 relative error; all ten synthetic VJP modes have scaled error below 3.61e-15, two probes per mode, including synthetic boundary/floor cases. Natural sampled events contain no floor/boundary cases.

At the full checkpoint, rank-half versus full mean-logit product VJP has norm ratio 1.4980837793212165, relative difference 0.6337797319593742, cosine 0.9487380791448279; the shared category/brand embedding VJP has norm ratio 1.053495212768841, relative difference 0.1563018947792516, cosine 0.9897633239987006. Rank-adjacent differences are smaller (product 0.1389281376801338, embedding 0.019811921013951118). At the half checkpoint, corresponding half differences are 0.5607598428134419 and 0.1639947210932855 versus adjacent 0.11652242937262229 and 0.02083977335714413. Each comparison is within one common checkpoint; the two checkpoints are learned outcomes.

Scale-half audit exceeds full by 0.00012049732767249743 AUC and reduces Logloss by 0.000030823655909423264, but loses both metrics on empty/1-16 histories and frequency_1_2. It beats full in 15/23 AUC and 16/23 loss slices; these overlapping exploratory slices are not independent replications.

Both audits have 17130275 parameters, 17078688 embedding and 51587 dense. Wall times are 615.1613 and 626.4336 seconds, training times 525.6302 and 535.3749 seconds; memory is 832739328 and 835099136 bytes. Cost differences are descriptive; allocated GPU seconds, exact training examples and controlled repeated latency are unexported.

interpretations.statement: The new audit supplies bounded common-state evidence of nonzero routing effects on product and shared embedding VJPs while preserving measured forward values. It addresses the previous missing-gradient-observation gap only for these first32 mean-logit probes.

interpretations.statement: Scalar scale first/second-moment conservation does not imply equality of the measured accumulated gradient: both norms and directions differ. This directly contradicts exact gradient equality for these probes, without establishing training update energy or an efficiency mechanism.
interpretations.qualification: The norms aggregate raw product gradients or unique shared embedding weights, which have different geometry and include other embedding routes.

interpretations.statement: Rank-adjacent stays much closer to full gradients than rank-half in the measured probes at both checkpoints, yet rank-half has the numerical AUC lead and rank-adjacent lower loss. A monotonic smaller-gradient-perturbation account of AUC superiority is not identified.
interpretations.qualification: The observed within-checkpoint ordering is not a controlled intervention on gradient distance alone; comparisons across checkpoints are descriptive.

interpretations.statement: Earlier temporal proximity/positive scale-correlation explanations remain insufficient. Rank-half has sampled own/donor scale correlation near -0.344 and retains the AUC lead, while chronological half loses. The rule/order matters provisionally; neither negative correlation nor temporal or action semantics is identified as causal.

The audit reduces concern that the added diagnostic path changed aggregate training results, but deterministic replay and algebraic probe consistency do not establish independent replication, population-wide isolation or reliable improvement.

No new training mechanism or forward architecture was introduced in round13. Its contribution is measurement of already executed backward rules. Literature priority and general mechanism superiority remain unverified.
